correctness.rationale: The torus map has kernel {0,(1/2,1/2)}, is surjective, and has absolute Jacobian two. The area formula gives half the sum of the sheet densities almost everywhere; normalized Haar is attained exactly when the sum is two. Equivalently the dual pulls back (k,ℓ) to (k+ℓ,k−ℓ), the full same-parity lattice. Copula marginals kill nonconstant axis modes. The only remaining modes of total degree at most two are (±1,±1), so there is no lower-degree nonconstant witness. At degree three, f(u)g(v)=sin(2πu)sin(4πv) cancels between the sheets, has both marginal integrals zero, and with 0<ε<1 gives strict positivity. Its CDF perturbation is ε times the product of the nonnegative primitives F and G, and swapping (1/4,1/8) distinguishes the density from its transpose. The first moments of the sines are −1/(2π) and −1/(4π), giving Spearman 3ε/(2π²). In the Kendall integral the two linear terms are each ε/(8π²) and the quadratic term vanishes since ∫Ff=∫Gg=0. The half-L¹ distance equals 2ε/π². The retained moment cos(2π(−U+2S)) has mean −ε/4 by expanding cos(2π(U+2V)). Identical oracle image laws give identical product laws and rejection probabilities, with no claim about ranks.
residual_risks: The lower-degree result uses total Fourier degree for trigonometric polynomials, not another degree convention or an arbitrary notion of smoothness. The exact power statement is for independent paired oracle observations only; the integration checks in the supplied script were not executed.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Raw independence cannot give this oracle counterexample. If raw S₀=U+V and D₀=U−V were independent, m=ess sup|D₀| would force S₀∈[m,2−m] a.s. from |D₀|≤min(S₀,2−S₀). Both mod-one laws uniform would then require 2m≥1 and 2−2m≥1, hence m=1/2. On those two unit intervals modulo one is a.e. bijective, so both raw variables would be independent uniforms, making (S₀+D₀)/2 triangular rather than uniform. Thus a theorem confined to raw independence cannot cover the displayed witness; whether the chapter discusses separately wrapped variables remains unverified.

value.rationale: The paired observable appears to carry more information than either of the summaries used for angular independence testing. A strictly positive analytic and positively quadrant-dependent counterexample shows the information loss persists even when both summary values are retained and dependence is positive by multiple criteria. The sharp first Fourier degree pinpoints that loss, and the oracle qualification prevents overreading it as a result on rank-based power.
